A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to evolve a simple braking task in a 2D environment with one stationary object using a simple neural controller.
the agents have evolved a strategy to stop as close to the object as possible, and that the agents are using an impulsive braking mechanism.

we are interested in how agents can be evolved to perform a simple braking task, how the agents' strategies depend on the information they perceive, how the agents can be evolved in more realistic environments, and how the agents' braking strategies can be improved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
impulsive braking strategies are robust across many different types of visual information.

the evolved agents use a strategy that is very similar to the strategy that is used by humans, and that the strategy is affected by optical variables in a way that is similar to the effects of optical variables in humans.

the impulsive braking strategy is not an artifact of the environment or the evolutionary algorithm, but is a strategy that emerges naturally from the interplay between the agent's perceptual capabilities, the agent's motor capabilities, and the task at hand.
